name: Felix
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: If none of this is true, and what we teach is heresy, they wouldn’t go to these great lengths and spend all this money. “And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way”: like Katt Williams said, the liar knows the lie he told. Felix knew exactly what Paul was teaching.

“And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled”. Paul told him of righteousness, the commandments, of temperance, and of the judgment to come. If the judgment Paul taught were foolishness, like a black man coming out of the sky, Felix would have said, you’re just crazy. Instead he trembled. That is why Esau is crazy over us on the street corners: he hears Revelation 2:9 and it clicks, I have to get payback. As James said, the devils also believe, and tremble.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org

cases.name: Felix the governor
cases.charge: Trembling at the judgment to come, hoping for a bribe, and leaving a man he knew to be innocent bound
cases.preview: Felix already had a more perfect knowledge of that way when he deferred the hearing (Acts 24:22).
